rv.q: True, it may take a few minutes to process the process, as it were. A mild case of sensory overload may have you reeling in the opening minutes, as you adjust to the necessity of taking it all in, and figuring out where to focus your concentration at any given moment.

This bold musical adaptation of Frank Wedekind's 1891 play about teenage sexual awakening is a powerhouse of raw emotion and contemporary relevance that should connect strongly with younger audiences.
Spring Awakening, a spiky hothouse bloom, drags not only Wedekind’s play but musical theater itself firmly into the now.
Spring Awakening is a musical of exceptional power and beauty, a show that succeeds in making the late 19th century feel urgently contemporary.
Spring Awakening — the breathtaking discussion of what it means to grow up — will become both a high mark of the season and a landmark musical.
Sheik’s absolutely haunting and often breathtaking score still outshine Sater’s poetic lyrics, and many of these songs clearly stand up to repeated listening.
That you leave the theater humming those songs rather than being devastated by what they mean is precisely what keeps Spring Awakening snowbound.

cn.t: Critics hail this original musical as an exhilarating landmark, praising its powerful rock score and raw exploration of teen sexuality. Most find it a breathtaking high mark for Broadway, though not all embrace its intensity.

vs.sum: The Eugene O'Neill Theatre offers decent sightlines, though some seats may have minor obstructions due to the shallow rake. Sound quality is generally good, ensuring an enjoyable auditory experience. While the comfort level is typical for Broadway, with standard legroom and seat width, the theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant Georgian design. Facilities are adequate, with bars and merchandise available on both levels, though restroom capacity may be limited during peak times.

acc.note: No elevators. All accessible seating on Orchestra level. Infrared headsets and audio induction neck loops.
